title: UK Establishes National Agentic Security Unit in £700 Million AI Budget
summary:
Chancellor John Healey has earmarked funds for a new regulatory body tasked with monitoring and responding to misaligned AI activity as part of a broader national security initiative. The National Agentic Security Unit will receive £40 million to investigate rogue agents, while the government will provide £60 million for an automated AI Cyber Shield and £70 million to identify security holes in the nation's critical infrastructure.

The wider investment package includes an additional £500 million for AI safety and £140 million for the Sovereign AI Unit. To reach a target of 6 GW of AI data-center capacity by 2030, the UK will offer strategic sites priority electricity grid access and temporary on-site power if the companies cover energy costs, report annual water usage, and invest in local communities.

🚨BREAKING: The UK is establishing a £40 MILLION National Agentic Security Unit to detect, investigate and respond to ROGUE AI agents.

Its new Budget calls for “world-first” capabilities against “misaligned agentic activity,” including monitoring and incident response.

And in the SAME £700M+ AI package:

>£60M for an AI-powered Cyber Shield to automate cyberdefence
>£70M for AI to identify vulnerabilities across critical infrastructure

Britain says it needs 6 GW of AI data-centre capacity by 2030. Strategic sites could get priority grid access and, exceptionally, temporary on-site power, in return for covering added energy costs, investing locally and reporting annual water use.

AI agents are becoming both the threat and the defence.
